historical_transitions.summary: Controller Gnosis Safe 0x570cE31D1309bb145DD3736B48c7328cc13f7e85 created via SafeSetup with 6 owners (0xee1bb6c8, 0xfd2786a8, 0x90bfc658, 0xf8c866f0, 0x50f72c67, 0x7e70b3cd) and threshold 3 (3-of-6), one day before the SteerPeriphery deployment batch it would come to control.

SteerPeriphery TransparentUpgradeableProxy deployed by EOA 0x48d915f4e17f7b1ca02cb13649a80bfc34f5aa63 with EIP-1967 implementation 0x45e039fa10c9540a6323f654484329775e7476fb, ProxyAdmin 0xEb2D829FFbE494FC6535b0E4EB807EFd4b6BF0Bd in the admin slot, and initialize() setting the periphery owner to the deployer EOA.

One block after deployment, periphery owner() was transferred from deployer EOA 0x48d915f4e17f7b1ca02cb13649a80bfc34f5aa63 to the 3-of-6 controller Safe 0x570cE31D1309bb145DD3736B48c7328cc13f7e85, which has held the periphery owner role ever since.

ProxyAdmin 0xEb2D829FFbE494FC6535b0E4EB807EFd4b6BF0Bd (itself deployed that morning at block 21,701,061) was transferred from the deployer EOA to the same Safe, completing a zero-timelock upgrade chain — Safe to ProxyAdmin to periphery proxy — with no TimelockController anywhere in the path.

Controller Safe signer rotation inside one execTransaction: RemovedOwner 0xfd2786a8928a155d8f9f2f0e0bfda016827b78d5 and AddedOwner 0x8710234d33ba31fceccebe405b92cdc3edc59aaa, preserving the 6-owner set and the threshold of 3 (3-of-6).

A single Safe execTransaction batch upgraded three Steer proxies at once; the periphery implementation rotated 0x45e039fa10c9540a6323f654484329775e7476fb to 0xac7d3a933c44b4d4bad6d5f0685900482e0d995e with zero delay. The incoming implementation had been exact-match verified on Sourcify on 2026-07-08, one day before execution.
RemovedOwner 0xee1bb6c88ec20e42ddf577970cbc897b979899e8 shrank the controller Safe from 6 to 5 owners while the threshold stayed at 3 (3-of-5), five days before the threshold itself was lowered.

ChangedThreshold lowered the controller Safe quorum from 3 to 2; combined with the August 2026 owner removal, the periphery upgrade path has since required only 2-of-5 signers, still with no timelock delay.

Pinned checkpoint at block 26,463,853: the EIP-1967 implementation slot still reads 0xac7d3a933c44b4d4bad6d5f0685900482e0d995e, periphery owner() is still the controller Safe, and Safe getThreshold() still returns 2 across 5 owners — no control-plane change since 2026-09-01.

evidence_sources.claim_summary: Archived official governance page: proposals pass signal and implementation votes, and 'A proposal can only be executed after the Timelock period has ended', with Governor Bravo tooling (Tally, Snapshot, Boardroom) listed as the governance model.

Live governance page, unchanged in substance: timelock-gated execution and a 40% quorum for token-holder governance, with no mention of the Safe-plus-ProxyAdmin path that actually upgrades the Ethereum SteerPeriphery proxy.

Hashlock final audit report (audit month March 2025) scoped to three Stryke LP manager contracts (StrykeLPManager, StrykeLPManagerV2, StrykeSteerLib) at GitHub commit 17db3aeffb541007f77d54c16bd50a4cf2ae313a; the SteerPeriphery proxy, its ProxyAdmin and the controller Safe were outside the audited scope.

Official SteerPeriphery API reference documents createVaultAndDepositGas, createVaultAndStrategy and deposit as the live periphery surface, matching the deployed implementation, but documents no timelock, governor or quorum gate on periphery upgrades.

gap_windows.summary: Documented governance promises timelock-gated, quorum-based execution, but the Ethereum periphery proxy's upgrade chain — controller Safe (3-of-6 at completion, 2-of-5 since 2026-09-01) acting through ProxyAdmin 0xEb2D829FFbE494FC6535b0E4EB807EFd4b6BF0Bd — has had zero timelock delay since the chain was completed at block 21,701,269; the 2026-07-09 implementation upgrade executed instantly inside one Safe transaction, and the governance documentation remains uncorrected 665.09 days later.

The official MultiPositionLiquidityManager documentation describes the initialize() parameter _steer as 'The steer multisig address, responsible for some governance functions'; at block 21,701,099 the periphery owner() reads exactly the controller Safe 0x570cE31D1309bb145DD3736B48c7328cc13f7e85, so the documented multisig role matches chain state at deployment.

executive_risk_memo: Steer Protocol's Ethereum control plane, reconstructed block by block from January 2025 to November 2026, shows steady centralisation drift behind reassuring documentation. The SteerPeriphery proxy (0xCEBF1A54A9Ce703FC80967760b5A6cbDb4111099; $12,197,359 DefiLlama TVL) was deployed on 2025-01-25 with implementation 0x45e039fa10c9540a6323f654484329775e7476fb, and within two blocks every lever of control — periphery owner() and ownership of ProxyAdmin 0xEb2D829FFbE494FC6535b0E4EB807EFd4b6BF0Bd — sat with a single Gnosis Safe (0x570cE31D1309bb145DD3736B48c7328cc13f7e85) created the previous day at 3-of-6. No TimelockController has ever gated this chain. The Safe rotated one signer in December 2025, upgraded the periphery implementation instantly on 2026-07-09 inside a three-proxy batch transaction, removed a sixth owner in August 2026, and lowered its own threshold to 2-of-5 on 2026-09-01. Each step reduced the coordination needed for a unilateral upgrade, while the official governance documentation continued to describe quorum-based, timelock-delayed token-holder governance — a documentation gap now open for 665.09 days without repair, and no Snapshot space or public proposal record ratifies any of these control changes. Two mitigations deserve credit: the July 2026 implementation was exact-match verified on Sourcify one day before execution, so the incoming code was publicly inspectable in advance, and the signer set has changed only twice since deployment. Engineering reality is thinner than the marketing surface suggests: the core periphery repository is not public, and the flagship public contract repository, SteerProtocol/vault-template, recorded only 3 commits by a single contributor in the trailing twelve months, a bus factor of 1 for publicly visible contract maintenance. Counterparties should price Steer exposure as instant-upgrade multisig risk — currently two signatures — not as the timelocked DAO governance the documentation describes.
